 SUIT FOR 
 
 THE SPECIFIC PERFORMANCE OF CONTRACT/AGREEMENT DATED 25 SEP 2020 WHEREBY THE DEFENDANT HAVE SOLD OUT A LAND MEASURING SITUATED IN ON A SALE CONSIDERATION OF AN AMOUNT OF RS. 1,14,93,739/- AND ADVANCE PAYMENT OF RS. 47, 41000/- WHILE ALL MONTHLY INSTALLMENT HAVE BEEN PAID AND NOTHING IS OUTSTANDING AGAINST THE PLAINTIFF TILL THE COMPLETION OF THE WHOLE AMOUNT INCLUDING COST OF THE CONSTRUCTION/SUPER STRUCTURE OVER THE PROPERTY IN QUESTION AND THE DEFENDANTS WERE UNDER LEGAL AND MORAL OBLIGATION TO HANDOVER PEACEFUL POSESSION OF THE SAME TO THE PLAINTIFF AND THE DEFENDANTS HAVE GOT NO RIGHT TO DENY THE TITLE OF THE PLAINTIFF AND ANY SUCH ACT OF DENIAL OR DELAY WILL BE WRONG, ILLEGAL AND INEFFECTIVE ON THE RIGHTS OF THE PLAINTIFF. 
 
 PERMANENT INJUCTION TO THE EFFECT OF RESTRAINING THE DEFENDANT THAT THE RESPONDENTS/DEFENDANTS AMY KINDLY BE RESTRAINED FROM SELLING OUT THE PROPERTY IN QUESTION, LEASING IT OUT, ALIENTING THE SAME, RENTING IT OUT OR TO DO ANYTHING PREJUDICIAL TO THE INTERSTS OF THE PLAINTIFF TILL THE FINAL DISPOAL OF THE ACCOMPYING SUIT. 
 
 MANDATORY INJUNCTION TO THE EFFECT THAT DEFENDANTS MAY KINDLY BE DIRECTED TO HANDOVER THE PROPERTY IN QUESTION TO THE PLAINTIFF WITHOUT ANY FURTHER DELAY OR ILLEGAL DEMANDS IN SHAPE OF EXTRA AMOUNT. 
 
 Written Statement on behalf of Defenda nt s 
 
 The Defen dant s most respectfully submits as under: 
 
 This written statement is be ing submitted by the M/s V4 Capital a Partnership Firm (hereinafter, the Defendant Firm ). This written statement is being submitted by the Defenda nt Firm through Mr. Syed Hasan Ali Shah who is fully conversant with the facts of the case and has been duly authorized in this behalf. 
 
 Preliminary Objections: 
 
 That the titled suit is bad for misjoinder of parties and is, therefore, liable to be dismissed forthwith. Zameen Ace Homes is not a legal entity, therefore, cannot be sued. 
 
 Th at a bare perusal of the plaint reveals that the Plaintiff has (i) failed to mention that he has any cause of action against any of the Defendants, (i i ) failed to add a paragraph relating to ‘suit valuation’ and court fees and ( iii ) failed to pay the requisite court fee under the Court Fees Act, 1870 . T he Plaint has been filed in utter disregard of the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 in particular its Orders IV, VI and VII , read with its Appendix A . Thus, the titled suit is not proceedable and is liable to be dismissed /rejected forthwith with exemplary costs. 
 
 That in addition , it is pertinent to mention that apparently the titled suit is a classic example of frivolous litigation and has been filed by the Plaintiff without any basis merely to avoid his contractual liabilities under the Agreement dated 25-09 -2020 (the ‘ Agreement ’) . Thus, the titled suit is liable to be rejected with exemplary costs. 
 
 Preliminary Submissions: 
 
 That the titled suit is me rely an attempt of the Plaintiff to deceive this learned Court and abuse the process of law by disguising his own failure to fulfill the contractual obligations arising out of the Agreement , whereby the Plaintiff agreed to purchase a Unit No. 3 S T-14 , measuring 133. Square Yard against a total sale consideration of PKR. 11,493,750 /- ( eleven million four h un dred ninety-three t housand seven hundred fifty only / - (henceforth the ‘ Purchase Price ’). 
 
 That under Clause 3 .3 of the Agreement , the Applicant was under an oblig ation to pay the adjusted price in case of any price escalation . Clause 3 .3 of the Agreement is being reproduced as under: 
 
 “ 3. PAYMENT 
 3.3 The purchase price of the purchased Unit shall remain fixed under this Agreement. However, the Purchase Price may be adjusted if, between the date of singing of this Agreement and the Completion Date, there is an increase in the price of Component Material, as per the price indices published by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics insofar as applicable, or if there is an increase in applicable Taxes or levy of any new Taxes. In this event, the Developer will make every reasonable effort for the Purchase Price to remain unaffected and ensure that any impact on the remaining Purchase Price is adjusted in a fair and reasonable manner (“Adjusted Amount”) . 
 
 The above clause is self - explanatory and clearly shows that the titled suit has been filed by the Plaintiff without any basis , merely to avoid his contractual liabilities under the Agreement. The titled suit is liable to be dismissed with exemplary costs on this score alone .

 Versus 
 
 Zameen ACE Homes etc. 
 
 
 APPLICATION FOR GRANT OF TEMPORARY INJUCTION TO THE EFFECT THAT THE DEFENDANT /RESPONDENTS MY KINDLY BE RESTRAINED FROM SELLING OUT THE PROPERTY IN QUESTION, LEASING IT OUT, ALIENTING THE SAME, RENTING IT OUT OR TO DO ANYTHING PREJUDICIAL TO THE INTERSTS OF THE PETITIONER/ PLAINTIFF TILL THE FINAL DISPOAL OF THE ACCOMPYING SUIT. 
 
 Reply on behalf of the Defendant s 
 
 PRELIMINARY OBJECTIONS: 
 
 That the contents of the Written Statement may kindly be read as an integral part of this Reply on behalf of the Defendant Firm. 
 
 That it is settled principle of law that there are three essential ingredients for grant of temporary injunction which must co-exist in favour of the party seeking it and in the instant case applicant/ plaintiff must show the prima facie case, balance of convenience in his favour and in case of non-grant of interim relief must prove irreparable loss. Thereafter, the court would require to see as to whether the applicant/plaintiff will suffer more inconvenience by withholding of the injunction as against the respondent/defendant. The court is required to weigh the mischief to either party i.e. to the applicant/plaintiff, if refused, and the respondent/defendant, if allowed, and will grant the injunction only if the balance is in favour of the applicant/plaintiff. Similarly, for getting injunction order, the applicant/plaintiff is bound to prove that in case of refusal of injunction he will suffer irreparable loss or injury. The term “Irreparable loss” does not refer to damage which cannot be physically repaired but to such material injury which cannot be adequately compensated. As the loss is ascertainable in terms of money, therefore, it is not a case of irreparable loss. As such where pecuniary compensation is an adequate relief, injunction will not be granted. Hence, the titled application is liable to be dismissed on this score alone. 
 
 That without prejudice to the above, if the application for grant of temporary injunction is allowed, it would amount to grant of main relief sought in the plaint. It is settled law that such like interim relief of temporary injunction cannot be granted, which amounts to grant of the final relief, or order passed creates altogether a different and new situation. Guidance can be taken from the case reported as “Islamic Republic of Pakistan through Secretary, Establishment division, Islamabad and others Vs Muhammad Zaman Khan and others” (1997 SCMR 1508), wherein it has been held that: “As regards the merits of the case, it may be pointed out that it is well settled proposition of law that the object of passing of an interlocutory order or status quo is to maintain the situation obtaining on the date when the party concerned approaches the Court and not to create a new situation. Another well-settled principle of legal jurisprudence is that generally a Court cannot grant an interlocutory relief of the nature which will amount to allowing the main case without trial/ hearing of the same.” The application under reply is liable to be dismissed on this score also. 
 
 PARAWISE REPLY: 
 
 The contents of Para No.1 need no reply. 
 
 The contents of Para No.2 are vehemently denied being baseless. The Plaintiff has no prima facie case in his favour. The application under reply is liable to be dismissed on this score alone. 
 
 The contents of Para No. 3 are vehemently denied being baseless. The application under reply is liable to be dismissed on this score also. 
 
 The contents of Para No. 4 are vehemently denied being frivolous. Plaintiff’s alleged loss, if at all any, is quantifiable in financial terms. It is trite law that any alleged loss, which is quantifiable in financial terms is not irreparable loss . The application under reply is liable to be dismissed on this score also. 
 
 PRAYER 
 
 Wherefore, it is respectfully prayed that the application under reply may very kindly be dismissed with exemplary costs including the cost of litigation, in the interest of justice.
